=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2754-2790 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `sleep "${settle_secs}"` runs before the peer-dedup check, so continuation runs can wait unnecessarily even when an in-flight peer already exists.
  WHY: All five reviewers identified the same ordering issue; it does not break correctness, but it wastes runner time when the later peer check would have exited anyway.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2754-2790 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Continuation-specific settle delay (`sleep "${settle_secs}"`) runs before the peer-dedup check, causing unnecessary wait when a peer run is already in flight
  WHY: When `is_continuation_dispatch="true"`, the workflow sleeps for settle delay (default 10s) then peer-wait (default 8s) before checking for in-flight peers via `autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer`; if a peer already exists, the workflow wastes up to 18 seconds of runner time before discovering it and exiting.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2754-2789 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `sleep "${settle_secs}"` is executed before the peer-dedup check.
  WHY: When a `pull_request.synchronize` event and a `workflow_dispatch` retrigger occur simultaneously, the `autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer` check is designed to skip the dispatch, but the runner still waits for the full 10-60 seconds before determining that a peer is already running and exiting.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~27,754-27,789 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The continuation-specific settle delay (`sleep "${settle_secs}"`) runs BEFORE the peer-dedup check (`autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer`).
  WHY: If an in-flight peer run already exists from the prior `synchronize` event, the workflow still waits the full settle period before exiting; this is an efficiency issue, not a correctness bug.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`:2754-2789 region | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `sleep "${settle_secs}"` (settle delay) runs BEFORE the peer-dedup check, so when an in-flight peer already exists the workflow still waits the full settle period before detecting it and exiting.
  WHY: The current code waits for settle delay, then peer wait, then checks for an in-flight peer; this wastes about 10s (configurable up to 60s) of runner time when a parallel run already exists, but does not affect correctness.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2756-2763,2784-2799 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Continuation settle delay executes before peer-dedup check, causing unnecessary runner wait when an in-flight peer will cause the dispatch to be skipped.
  WHY: The `sleep "${settle_secs}"` is inside the continuation flag block and happens before `autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer`; the peer check should occur first so the settle delay is only paid when dispatch will proceed.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
